doc.title: Earl Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002

title: Hampton's band in San Francisco; low road pay
summary: Musicians loved San Francisco's theater scales; on the road they were paid little and paid their own hotels.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Yes. So he got with Lionel. Yeah that was a band. They always, the musicians loved to come to San Francisco. See he would come here and do the Golden Gate Theater, do their show there. He would do that, oh man he was a regular there. And the men loved to come to San Francisco because we had one of the highest theater scales. Yes. So when they’d come here they’d be downtown buying socks, underwear, shirts. Because when they were on the road they didn’t make very much. Now Quincy Jones in his autobiography he mentions his stint with Lionel and he said they were making fifteen dollars a night. So I’ve forgotten the year he mentioned. But that wasn’t very much money.
Right. And sometimes you’d have to pay your own food.
Well you did, you paid your own hotel, and your own restaurant. Yeah.
